Re-read live Part marker and spawn/player start pixels; fixed frame inputs are valid only if the current MAME identity and deterministic startup sequence match the retained calibration.
Use existing scripts/capture_mame_gameplay.py JSON planner. Do not write arcade memory or add runtime-control machinery.

phase.name: Part-1 free-junction input-versus-neutral and perpendicular-axis calibration
phase.success_marker: Part counter $606E=1; exact player pixel template and RAM coordinates at source-proven free node (12,14); no displacement during the neutral baseline; then an Up-held eastward legal maze_nav edge from that same node.
phase.timeout_meaning: Required live junction/axis marker was not observed in the bounded phase; not evidence that the game is slow.
fail_if: Part counter changes or player dies before the measured segment.
RAM and pixel origin disagree beyond the calibrated sprite-origin transform.
The player moves during the implicit no-directional-input baseline at frames 684-689.
Up-held segment does not traverse the expected legal maze_nav edge.
Input segment begins in the forced spawn corridor or at an unverified node.
